messages:
jamie_acme: Hey team — after we migrated some services to `redwood-embed-v2` we're seeing intermittent embedding length mismatches. Some responses are 1536 dims, others 1024. Downstream code assumes 1024 and crashes. Started after a deploy yesterday.

nina_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl + response) and any request ids? are you using our SDK or direct REST? also does this correlate with a particular tenant/account?

jamie_acme: we're calling REST API directly. repro below (redacted API key):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v2","input":["foo","bar","baz"],"batch_size":64}'
```

Response snippet: (one request where first vector is 1536)
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[... length 1536 ...]},{"embedding":[... length 1536 ...]},{"embedding":[... length 1536 ...]}],"model":"redwood-embed-v2","usage":{}}
```

Other requests immediately afterwards return 1024. We see this happening ~1/200 requests, no clear pattern. Request-IDs: `r-0a1b2c3d`, `r-0a1b2c3e`.

nina_support: thanks — can you confirm whether you set a custom `cache_prefix` or `X-Redwood-Cache-Prefix` header? and are you sharding by tenant id in your client?

jamie_acme: we don't set any cache header explicitly. we assume Redwood isolates by account. we do reuse the same client across multiple internal services that sometimes call different models (v1 vs v2).

omar_runtime: pinging runtime — quick note: we recently shipped a subtle change in cache key derivation that fell back to a shared prefix when the `model` field was omitted from an SDK payload. if a client reuses the same connection across different model variants the prefix could collide and return embeddings cached for a different model/shape. that would explain mixed dims.

lucy_sre: omg that matches the pattern — low frequency, across tenants using pooled clients. jamie, can you confirm if any callers omit the explicit `model` field or send `model` in headers only? also what's your observed batch_size during hits?

jamie_acme: we do have a legacy path that sets model via header `X-Model-Name` for some callers, so occasionally the body lacks `model`. batch_size is variable; most failures seen when batch_size > 32.

nina_support: ok, root cause hypothesis: cache key fallback + header-only model = prefix reuse across model variants -> cached vectors with different dimension. Workarounds while we patch: 1) explicitly include `model` in request body 2) set a unique `cache_prefix` per tenant/service 3) reduce batch_size to avoid mixing cached and freshly computed vectors.

jamie_acme: can you show an example header to force namespace?

nina_support: yes — add header `X-Redwood-Cache-Prefix: acme-service-1` or in body `{ "cache_prefix": "acme-service-1" }`. That will avoid shared keys.

omar_runtime: engineering plan: we're hotpatching the cache key derivation to require (tenant_id + model + quantization) and not fall back to global. patch scheduled in the next deploy window. I'll add an internal flag to force cache eviction on the affected hosts.

deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy: runtime/cache-key-fix @ 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z (rolling, 10 hosts). Change: include `model` in canonical cache key.

kevin_billing: FYI — this cache bug could have inflated charges if clients repeatedly computed embeddings instead of hitting cache. we'll monitor for unusual billing variance for accounts that reported issues. jamie, if you want a billing review ping me and we'll make sure there are no surprises.

jamie_acme: thanks — I'll enable explicit `cache_prefix` and ensure `model` in body across callers. we'll also run a short canary. please keep me posted and attach the deploy link.

nina_support: tracked as SUP-2026-1123. we'll follow up after the hotfix and verify your reported request IDs. thanks for the quick repro, that really helped. :pray:
summary: Customer reported intermittent embedding dimension mismatches traced to cache-prefix fallback when model was not specified in body; engineering hotfix scheduled; suggested workarounds and billing follow-up.
